POREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Chemical Hazards Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. Ethyl Ether has a wide range of uses. It is a good solvent for many organic substances among which are oils, fats, gums, resins, certain select nitrocelluloses, perfumes and alkaloids. A mixture of ethyl ether and ethyl alcohol has excellent solvent properties for nitrocelluloses and Another important use of ethyl ether is as an is used in large quantities for this purpose. extracting medium for the concentration of acetic and other organic acids. It is used as a reaction medium in Wurtz and Grignard syntheses, as a starting fuel for diesel engines, and as Ethyl ether is used as a an entrainer for dehydration of ethyl alcohol and isopropyl alcohol general anesthetic in surgery. It is a colourless, volatile and highly flammabIe liquid with a sweet pungent odour. is miscible with ethyl alcohol, oils and the usual organic solvents in all proportions. In the preparation of this code of safety, following publications: considerable assistance Ethyl ether from the

4.2.7 MiscibilitylSolubility The solubility of ethyl ether in water at 20�C is 6.8 percent by mass and that of water in ethyl ether at 20�C is 1.2 percent by mass. It is miscible with ethyl alcohol, oils and the usual oils and the usual organic solvents in all proportions. 4.2.8 Vapour Density 4.3 Chemical Properties Although ether is relatively unreactive, like ethers in general a few of its reactions are worth noting. The spontaneous formation of non-volatile peroxides on standing in air, especially in the light is important from the stand point of the resultant hazards. The peroxide remains as a residue when ether evaporates and may explode violently in a Weak acids distillation carried out to dryness. or water bring about peroxide decomposition to hydrogen peroxide and ethyl alcohol.

5.3 It is absorbed almost instantly from the lungsand verypromptlyfrom the intestinal tract. It undergoes no chemical change in the body. The maximum safe atmospheric concentrations of ethyl ether for prolonged exposure have not been determined under industrial conditions. 5.4 It is not safe for individual to inhale or ingest vapDurs of ether. It is not toxic in the sense of being a poison. Tt is however, a depressant of the central nervous system (CNS) of producing intoxication, and is capable drowsiness, stupor, and unconsciousness. Death due to respiratory failure may result from over exposure. 6 PERSONAL 6.1 Respiratory a) Gas mask with approved organic vapour canister ( for minor leakages and spills ), and b) Self contained respirator. 6.2 Non-respiratory a) Hand gloves and neoprene or butyl b) Safety c) Full cover apron rubber. made of PVC, glass. or rubber breathing or air line PRO'TECTIVE EQUIPMENT

7.1.3 All electrical wirings, light fittings, motors installed or used where ethyl ether is handled or stored should bc essentially flame proof type only. All storage tanks should be fitted with a vent pipe/breather. All plant and machinery handling ethyl ether shall be effectively earthed for controlling undesirable static electricity. Structural steel work shall be effectively carlhed with plant/equipm?nt b3nded to the structural steel work. 7.1.4 Bulk storage areas should bc away from the sources of open flame, heaters, furnaces and welding or other flame or spark-producing equipments. `NO SMOKING' signs should be conspicuously displayed in the area. All storage tanks should be grounded and provided with continuous water sprinkler arrangements for cooling. Joints in the pipelines used for transporting ethyl ether should be bonded. 7.2 Handling 7.2.1 The area where ethyl ether is handled should be declnrcd as a class I hazard location. 7.2.2 All equipment used for maintenance purposes should be made of non-sparking metal alloys. Utmost care should be exercised while loading and unloading ether by employing carefully instructeti and reliable personnel. 7.3 Label@ 7.3.1 Hazard warning symbols/labels should bc displayed in the plant areas. Cautionary/ warning notices such as "SMOKING AND NAKED FLAME VERY STRICTLY PROHIBTTED. SPILLAGE BE AVOI DEED" may be displayed. 7.3.2 Labels of conl:tincrs following details : a) Name of material; b) Vapour hazardous able; and c) Keep away flame. 8.1 Waste mixtures containing dicthyl ether should not be allowed to enter drains or sewers may result. The where serious explosions following methods are recommended for disposal. For obvious reasons of fire hazard, spillage of ethyl ether should be carefully avoided. 8.2 There should be adequate arrangement fol collection of spills or leaks of ethyl ether and for destruction by burning. There should be arrangement for water washing of floors/areas. Letting out ethyl ether waste into municipal drains, sewers directly or 10 the earth or undcrground water should be avoided. 8.3 Contaminated carlh, sand or absol-bent materials shall be collected :tnd chemically treated over a period until they are rendered safe for disposal. Alternatively, the contaminatcd materials may bc incinerated. 9 FIRE PREVENTLON AND FIRE FlGHTING

11.1 In case of skin contacts the contaminated cIothing are removed. The skin is washed thoroughly with water. 11.2 In case of contact with eyes, the eyes are flushed thoroughly with water for at Ieast 15 minutes. No lotion or ointment may be applied. The physician is to be contacted if irritation/ inflammation persists. 11.3 In case of exposure to high concentrations resulting in narcotic symptoms the patient is shifted to an uncontaminated area at once. If breathing is difficult artificia1 respiration should be administered and a physician called in. 11.4 Emergency Actions
